title: Compactness with rational coefficients
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$
([def-weil-finite-field-fiber]), and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Fix $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite subextension
$\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb$, and let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Use the condensed
coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled
back to $\Lambda_X$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $X$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme, the standing geometric setting of [sk-def-sf-setting].
Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves and
$\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ for the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology
([sk-def-sfb-constructible]). Let $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ be the full subcategory of
$\Mod(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$ consisting of filtered colimits of objects of
$\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, and put
$$
\Dic(X,\Lambda)=\{K\in D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda):
H^r(K)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\text{ for every }r\in\mathbf Z\}.
$$
Here the ambient category is the ordinary unbounded derived category
$D(\Mod(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Ab),\Lambda_X))$ of
$\Lambda_X$-module sheaves, the layer-(B) row of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].
The symbols $\Cons$ and $\Dbc$ throughout this statement retain the finite constant
local-model constructibility convention of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; the separate
$D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ row of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], defined using arbitrary
local finite presentations, is not used to define these symbols. Write $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ for the
smallest full triangulated subcategory of this ambient category that is closed under
isomorphisms, contains $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$, and is closed under all small ambient
coproducts [det-def-localizing-closure-existence]. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is
compact in this closure, with compactness as in [def-pc-compact-object]. More precisely,
for $C\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and every small family $(K_\lambda)$ in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$,
the canonical map, induced by the coprojections, is an isomorphism:
$$
\bigoplus_\lambda\Hom(C,K_\lambda)\longrightarrow
\Hom\Bigl(C,\bigoplus_\lambda K_\lambda\Bigr).
$$
All Hom groups and coproducts in this formula are computed in the ambient derived category.

proof.text: Use the layer-(B) ambient-category row of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] to identify $D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$ with the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\Mod(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Ab),\Lambda_X))$. The coefficient ring is the pulled-back commutative condensed ring fixed in the statement. Constructibility in $\Cons$ and $\Dbc$ is the convention fixed in this item; this identification uses only the ambient-category row, not the separate $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ row. Work in $\mathcal T=\Dic(X,\Lambda)$, with the Hom groups inherited from the ambient derived category. For [det-ambient-ind-derived-triangulated], our field has characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, $X$ is separated of finite type over it, and $E\subseteq\Qlb$ is the chosen finite subextension; its module, constructibility and universe conventions are those fixed above. Therefore it gives that $\mathcal T$ is a full triangulated subcategory. By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums] it is closed under small direct sums and both canonical truncations, and contains $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$. The ambient sums exist by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](1). An ambient sum of objects of this full subcategory has the same universal property within it, so these are also the sums of $\mathcal T$. Consequently [def-pc-compact-object] identifies the displayed comparison, for all small families in $\mathcal T$, with compactness of $C$ in $\mathcal T$.

source.place: First paragraph: ambient sums and inclusion of the localizing closure; formulate the stronger assertion as compactness in Dic

proof.text: Fix a constructible sheaf $C$. Obtain a nonnegative uniform Ext bound $d_C$ from [sk-lem-uniform-constructible-ext], transporting the Ext universe by the injective canonical change-of-universe equivalence. Put $T_C=\tau_{\geq-d_C}\tau_{\leq0}$, using the ordinary derived t-structure truncations of [def-kun-truncations]. By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums], these truncations and ambient sums preserve $\mathcal T$. For the truncation comparison, use the existing proved instance DerivedCategory.preservesColimitsOfShape_homologyFunctor in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.HomologyCoproducts: the coefficient module heart is Grothendieck abelian and has K-injective resolutions and exact coproducts. The coproduct of objects in degrees at least $a$ is again in degrees at least $a$, by preservation of homology. The universal property of truncGE therefore constructs an inverse to its coproduct comparison, with both inverse equations checked on coprojections. For truncLE, write the coproduct of its canonical inclusions as the composite of its coproduct comparison with the canonical inclusion on the sum. In degrees $n\leq a$, the homology maps of the inclusions are isomorphisms, and preservation of coproducts makes the homology of their sum an isomorphism; cancel the inclusion on the sum. In degrees $n>a$, both sides have zero homology. DerivedCategory.isIso_iff, the cohomology criterion in the ordinary localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], proves that this comparison is invertible. Thus both truncations, and hence $T_C$, preserve the required coproducts, compatibly with their coprojections. The good-truncation bounds place every $T_CK_\lambda$ in the common interval $[-d_C,0]$.

source.place: Third paragraph: the common truncation interval and compatibility with direct sums

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-finite-window] only with $m=0$, both to each $K_\lambda$ and to their sum. Its current statement explicitly places the constructible source in degree zero and takes Hom in the same ordinary derived category of pulled-back condensed coefficient modules; our $d_C\geq0$ and membership hypotheses were established in Steps 1–2. Its natural isomorphisms identify $\Hom(C,K)$ with $\Hom(C,T_CK)$. By their naturality and Step 2 the square whose top row is the comparison for $(K_\lambda)$ and whose bottom row is the comparison for $(T_CK_\lambda)$ commutes; the vertical arrows are isomorphisms. Every object in the bottom family has cohomology in the same interval $[-d_C,0]$. For the application of [det-constructible-compactness-bounded], the standing field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$. Our coefficient symbols denote exactly its condensed rings $\underline E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$, with $E$ viewed as a finite subextension of the chosen algebraic closure in the coefficient convention; our ambient category is its ordinary $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, with no derived-completion condition. The family is indexed by a small set in the fixed universe, $C$ is a constructible sheaf in degree $0$, and $-d_C\leq0$ because $d_C\geq0$. Its $\IndCons$ and $\Dic$ are the categories defined in the statement of this item. Thus apply its comparison $\alpha_0$ to the family $(T_CK_\lambda)$ with $a=-d_C$, $b=0$, $s=0$. This is exactly the bottom row, since $\alpha_0$ sends a finitely supported tuple to the sum of its composites with the coprojections. Therefore the bottom row is an isomorphism. Thus the top row is an isomorphism. The family was arbitrary, so every constructible sheaf $C$ is compact in $\mathcal T$ by [def-pc-compact-object]. No common bound on the original family is assumed.

source.place: Second and third paragraphs: use the uniformly bounded-family result, then the m=0 finite-window reduction

proof.text: Compact objects of the full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal T$ form a triangulated, isomorphism-closed class by [lem-sc-compact-objects-thick], since Step 1 supplies its coproducts. Map this class to the ambient derived category along the full inclusion. The existing proved lemma DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TStructure applies to this image and the isomorphism-closed constructible heart property of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Its degree-zero hypothesis is exactly Step 3. Its boundedness and homology hypotheses are exactly the definition of $\Dbc$. The lemma performs finite Postnikov induction using the canonical t-structure truncation triangles: the lower tail is zero, the successive layers are shifts of cohomology, and triangulated closure supplies the induction step. This retains the unit's finite-extension argument while reusing the already proved library induction instead of the separate complex-representative theorem lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle. It gives an object of $\mathcal T$ isomorphic to $C$, compact there. Fullness lifts the ambient isomorphism to $\mathcal T$, and isomorphism closure transports compactness to $C$. Step 1 now identifies it with the displayed ambient comparison for every bounded constructible $C$.

source.place: Final paragraph: shifts, triangles and the finite Postnikov induction; Stacks Tags 09QH and 08J5

proof.text: Finally $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))\subset\mathcal T$ by [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](3). Apply [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](2) with the actual class $\mathcal S=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and with the condensed coefficient ring fixed in our statement. It gives this full subcategory, closed under isomorphisms and ambient small direct sums, directly; no identification with the closure of $\Dctf$ is used. Hence for every family in that closure its coproduct and all Hom groups in the comparison are exactly the ambient ones, as in Step 1. The comparison proved in Step 4 is therefore also the compactness comparison inside $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$, proving the first assertion.

source.place: First paragraph: restrict the stronger assertion from Dic to the full localizing closure

proof_origin.place: All four paragraphs, implemented by U7 using the existing homology-coproduct API and DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded for the same finite Postnikov induction; Stacks 09QH and 08J5.

Made this distinction explicit in the statement and Step 1, and verified the expanded field, scheme, finite-subextension and universe hypotheses at the triangulated-subcategory application. Preserved the common-window truncation comparison, bounded-family specialization, finite Postnikov induction and direct localizing closure of Dbc. Refreshed current shared metadata, re-read all 18 distinct dependencies and certified all 19 step/use pairs. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves; no Lean work.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes paragraph 1 ambient setup; Steps 2–3 realize paragraphs 2–3 via det-constructible-compactness-bounded and the natural m=0 finite-window isomorphism; Step 4 realizes paragraph 4 using 09QH and successive truncation triangles; Step 5 concludes paragraph 1. The imported detail det-constructible-compactness-devissage states the whole conclusion, so it is recorded in same_as rather than used as a black-box proof. The final blueprint paragraph incorrectly asserts shift closure for a fixed target family: Hom(C[1],K_lambda)=Hom(C,K_lambda[-1]) involves a different family. Step 3 proves the comparison for all families, and Step 1 keeps the shifted family in Dic; Step 4 therefore applies 09QH to compactness quantified over all families before the finite Postnikov induction. This repairs that inference within the same shifts-and-triangles route.

There are no new nodes. Statement: the blueprint leaves X unbound; the item fixes k=F̄_q (sk-def-sf-setting), X separated of finite type, and Λ=E or Q̄_ℓ as the same condensed rings pulled back to Λ_X in ordinary D(Mod_{Λ_X}). Cons/Dbc follow sk-def-sfb-constructible, Dic is defined inline, Loc(Dbc) comes from localizing-closure-existence(2), and both conclusions are kept. Restricting k to F̄_q is necessary, not a weakening: uniform-ext is proved only there, and over a field with infinitely many nonzero H^n(k,Λ), C=Λ and K_n=Λ[n] give ∏ against ⊕, so the theorem fails. Step 1: the triangulated, sums(1-3) and localizing(1) hypotheses all hold, and the full subcategory inherits ambient coproducts. Step 2: the comparison of truncated sums is a morphism of complexes and a quasi-isomorphism on the window [-d_C,0]. Step 3: finite-window at m=0 has window [-d_C,0]; the bounded node applies with a=-d_C, b=0, s=0, its α_0 formula is the bottom row, and naturality makes the square commute. Step 4: the 09QH tool in Dic plus the successive truncation triangles give a finite induction from 0 to C; quantifying over all families repairs the blueprint's fixed-family shift wording. Step 5: Loc(Dbc) lies in Dic with the same Hom groups and sums. Small cases checked: empty family, zero source, d_C=0, one-degree source, empty X, unbounded families, Spec F̄_q. proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no cycle and no SGA. Accepted tool_uses: sk-lem-finite-window (named in the blueprint proof; the unit uses list omits it), sk-lem-uniform-constructible-ext, lem-sc-compact-objects-thick, lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle, def-kun-truncations. Devissage is correctly listed in same_as and not cited; the sheaf detail is proved inline. Unit realized fields are correct. For the maintainer: whoever splits det-brown-hypotheses-generation, which serves the arbitrary-field sk-lem-brown-hypotheses, must keep k=F̄_q. No fixes were written.

lean.statement: theorem constructible_compactness (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hℓ : ℓ ≠ D.p) (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ) (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] : HasConstructibleCompactness (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X ∧ HasConstructibleCompactness (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) X
lean.note: Both rational coefficients are conjuncts, using the canonical finite-subextension and algebraic-closure ring objects. HasConstructibleCompactness expands both assertions: IsCompactObject inside the full localizingClosure of the actual finite-constant-model Dbc class, and the canonical ambient Hom comparison for every small family whose cohomology lies in ObjectProperty.ind of the same constructibility predicate. The comparison is real data given by DirectSum.toAddMonoid of postcomposition with coprojections. No common bound, finite Tor amplitude or derived completeness is assumed.
